detail: cited in-web by 4; INSPIRE 207 as of 2026-08-21. Promoted from a stub on 2026-09-10, when the maintainer supplied the full 32-page scan of the published article and it was read in full. Part I of two: the printed title carries the "(I)", and section 1 states that Part II will give the MCV results on a 5^3 x 8 lattice using Wilson loops up to length 8. Euclidean quenched Monte Carlo throughout -- comparison only, nothing numerical enters any Hamiltonian claim. What the pinned pages actually carry, in three parts. (1) The operator classification the T_1^{+-} channel label comes from. Section 3 constructs every irreducible representation of the 48-element cubic group O_h on spacelike Wilson-loop operators up to length 8, and Table 3.1 (p. 120) prints the irreducible content of the four prototypes up to length 6. The single spatial plaquette, d = 6, decomposes as A_1^{++} + E^{++} + T_1^{+-} -- three C-even states and three C-odd ones -- and that C-odd triplet is the class the corpus's bare T_1^{+-} carrier belongs to. Section 3.2 states the rule that produces the split: real parts of Wilson-loop operators carry C = +1, imaginary parts carry C = -1. The transcription was checked here by summing the printed multiplicities against the printed dimension d, exactly, for all four prototypes: #1 plaquette 1 + 2 + 3 = 6; #2 double plaquette 1 + 1 + 4 + 3 + 3 = 12; #3 bent plaquette 12 (P = +) + 12 (P = -) = 24; #4 twisted plaquette 1 + 3 + 1 + 3 = 8. A second, independent check of the same transcription: applying the paper's own subduction assignment (eq. 3.6 -- A_1 -> 0, T_1 -> 1, E and T_2 -> 2, A_2 -> 3) to Table 3.1 yields ten distinct J^{PC} labels, nine of them excited, which is the count section 5 states and the set Table 8 tabulates. (2) The mass gap. m(0^{++}) = (280 +- 50) Lambda_L (eq. 4.6), about 750 MeV through Lambda_L = (6 +- 1) x 10^-3 sqrt(K) and sqrt(K) approximately 440 MeV (eqs. 4.7-4.8); the tangent method on the strong-coupling series gives 310 Lambda_L (eq. 4.9). A 4^3 x 8 lattice, Pietarinen heat bath, about 80 hours of CDC 7600. (3) The negative result, which is the part that matters here. The 0^{++} scaling window ends sharply at 5.6 < beta < 5.7, and there is no scaling window for any of the nine excited states: "we have no signal for the existence of any of these states in the physical spectrum" (section 5). Table 8 gives the 1^{+-} at distance t = 1, minimized over its contributing operators, as 4.87(44), 4.19(24), 4.33(16) and 4.56(41) at beta = 5.2, 5.4, 5.6 and 5.7 -- roughly flat in beta, which is the paper's own reading of it. A methodological finding recorded alongside: systematic-sweep upgrading produced significantly negative values for the positive-definite 0^{--} correlation (Table 9), and random-link upgrading, which satisfies detailed balance, removed the effect immediately. detail: cited in-web by 0. The arXiv nonexclusive-distrib grant runs to arXiv and not to this repository, so the copy is pinned by digest and never stored. The measurement: with (10087 +- 44) x 10^6 J/psi events, the decay X(2370) -> K*(892)^0 Kbar^0 + c.c. is searched for in J/psi -> gamma K0_S K0_S pi0 and not found. B[J/psi -> gamma X(2370)] x B[X(2370) -> K*(892)^0 Kbar^0 + c.c. -> K0_S K0_S pi0] = (0.1 +- 1.2(stat) +- 1.1(syst)) x 10^-6, hence < 2.7 x 10^-6 at 90 percent C.L.; the ratio to the inclusive K0_S K0_S pi0 mode is R = 0.003 +- 0.040(stat) +- 0.026(syst), hence R < 0.081 at 90 percent C.L. Because a 0^{-+} flavor singlet cannot decay to K*(892) Kbar by generalized G-parity, the suppression is read as a flavor-singlet signature, and the paper claims the X(2370) as the first flavor-singlet light hadron observed above 1 GeV/c^2. Supporting numbers as printed: the X(2370) mass 2376.3 +- 8.7(stat) +3.2/-4.3(syst) MeV/c^2 and width 83 +- 17(stat) +44/-6(syst) MeV from the 2011 discovery; J^{PC} = 0^{-+} determined at more than 9.8 sigma; the fit here fixes mass and width to the combined 2359 MeV/c^2 and 170 MeV. It quotes the lattice 0^{-+} ground-state glueball mass as 2.3 to 3.0 GeV/c^2 from its refs [1-6], and the lattice-predicted radiative production rate to the pure 0^{-+} glueball as (2.31 +- 0.90) x 10^-4 from its ref [5]. Why it is indexed here rather than left out as phenomenology: it is the experimental half of the identification problem G18 names, argued in the same shape. Its central mechanism is that the glueball is not itself the observed state -- a glueball/c-cbar mixing with a 2 to 5 degree angle raises the mixture's J/psi radiative production rate to (2-20) x 10^-3, one to two orders of magnitude above the pure glueball's, so "identification of the 0^{-+} glueball dominant mixture particle should be an unambiguous proof". A published, experimental statement that the object of interest is reached only through a dressed state, from a programme with no knowledge of this one. Bibliographic reading, from its own 39-entry reference list: the lattice anchors are Bali et al. 1993 [1], MP_1999 [2], CHEN_2006 [3], Gregory et al. 2012 [4], Gui et al. 2019 [5], Vadacchino 2023 [6], MORNINGSTAR_2025 [15] and Dudek et al. 2011 [39]. The LaTeX source of Hazra, "New class of exactly flat topological bands", indexed as LIT:HAZRA_2026. Set aside rather than imported because the submission's own front matter says "License information to appear upon publication". Read in full. It builds exactly flat bands from H = t B^T B on the faces of an arbitrary graph and proves the extensive null space topologically protected by a discrete Atiyah-Singer index theorem. The reading's load-bearing detail is a footnote and a definition: its B is the UNORIENTED face-vertex incidence, B_vf = 1 when vertex v lies on the face's cycle, so on the cubic lattice |V| = L^3, |F| = 3L^3 and the bound is 2L^3 by rank-nullity. This repository's face operator is the SIGNED face-edge boundary with |F| = |E|, index 0, and L^3 + 2 zero modes from homology. Same form, different mechanism -- the registered check states the distinction so the resemblance is not absorbed as a unifying candidate it could not falsify.

Importing it would pin a snapshot of the repository as though it were evidence about the repository. It is also already stale -- the shipped copy reports 2,215 nodes and 2,759 edges, where HEAD regenerates 2,329 and 3,069, so the bundle's own atlas no longer describes the graph it was rendered from. It plainly belongs to the open-cube VQE work the B = 4 validation cites, but the bundle carries no generating script, no caption, no axis units and no run record for it, so which Hamiltonian, cutoff and coupling convention produced these curves cannot be established from the bytes. Set aside rather than pinned into the B = 4 run directory, where it would sit beside re-derived certificates and read as though it had the same standing. The renormalized conditional score variance is exactly K_g(Q)=(1/4) integral r_g^2/p_g dy, where r_g=partial_g p_g+g^-1 Z_Q p_g+g^-1 div_y(p_g Z_y). Simultaneous conjugation invariance identifies this variance with K_g(w), w=tr(Q)/2.

S6-S7 identify the exact minimum graph m(q)=(q/4,q/4,q/2) and positive local conditional Gaussian Hessian. Potential and Agmon minima are connected by this proof, rather than identified by assumption. No differentiated ground asymptotics are asserted.

At regular fixed Q=exp(i theta n.sigma), both minima are attained uniquely by U0=U1=exp(i theta n.sigma/4) and U2=U3=exp(i theta n.sigma/2). The local conditional phase Hessian is positive near the unique well.
